findings.title: The cutover arms reconciliation after an explicitly unarmed run
findings.description: Description: The weekly job deliberately exits successfully with a `weekly backup done (unarmed)` line when the arm file is absent. `step_weekly` accepts that line because it checks only the `WEEKLY_DONE` prefix, then creates the arm file. This arms the destructive reconcile without the watched reconcile required by the setup instructions; a later weekly run can proceed with the offsite mirror. Require evidence of a successful armed reconcile before creating the arm file.

findings.title: Health checks can accept a stale clean log entry
findings.description: Description: `run_health` ignores the command’s return code and reads the latest line in the existing log without confirming that this invocation appended it. If the command fails before writing a log entry, a prior clean `FLAGS archive=0 stale=0` line can satisfy the cutover’s health checks. Verify that the invocation produced a fresh summary before using it.

findings.title: Check mode creates the rehearsal directory
findings.description: Description: `--check --rehearse` runs `mkdir -p "$REHEARSE"` before the check-mode actions. This mutates the filesystem despite the script’s documented `--check` no-changes contract. Avoid creating the rehearsal directory in check mode, or explicitly revise the contract and tests.
